extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - A new top bar, matching tofa's Apple TV app 2.0: the fox on its own, Home, Browse, Discover and Search as plain tabs, and Settings as a gear beside your profile picture. Select your profile picture to switch profiles. - Discover matches the Apple TV app too: Now, Acclaimed, Genres and Decades are plain tabs that switch as you move across them, the page uses the full width, and the row you are on stays in the same place as you scroll. - New Filters on Discover: hide watched movies, cinema-only movies or upcoming titles, or show only what is in your library. - The title page's second half is now one page you scroll through, as on the Apple TV app: the episode you are on with its synopsis, the seasons and episodes, then Cast & Crew, More Like This, More to Discover and an About card. The episode you are about to resume is no longer hidden as a spoiler, and Specials come after the last season. Its rows use smaller posters, as the Apple TV app's do. - Rows on Home and Discover are spaced like the Apple TV app's. - The player matches the Apple TV app 2.0: an episode's controls start with the episode list, the Playback button (a gauge) adds a Speed setting where Kodi allows it, and the stats button simply shows or hides the stats. - Next Up comes in four styles -- Compact, Minimal, Lower third and Full -- chosen for each TV under Settings > Playback & Video. - The stats name how a title is playing in words: Direct Play, Direct Stream or Transcode. - The pause screen and the episode list match the Apple TV app: pausing shows the year, episode and its title on their own lines, and the Episodes button opens a row of episodes along the bottom of the screen. - A title watched for less than a minute offers Play again, not Resume. - Settings matches the Apple TV app 2.0: its pages are tabs along the top, with a new Home tab, and This Device's settings now sit under Account and Privacy & About. The left side describes the setting you are on, every setting fits on one line, and its choices open in a list beside it -- Fox accent opens a grid of foxes. - On the Home tab, select a row to move it, hide it or remove one you added, and add a Discover or genre row from the two rows below. - Settings shows a preview for the playback rows, Fox accent and the Home tab, drawn over artwork from your own library. - Browse matches the Apple TV app 2.0: it opens on tiles for your libraries, Watchlist, History, Collections and Surprise me, and each opens full screen with seven posters across, the genres as a row of buttons, and an Unwatched switch beside Sort and Filter. - Collections shows your own collections first, then film series and sets, as wide cards three to a row; yours show four of their posters. - Sort opens as a panel over the view, with the current sort ticked and its direction shown; choose it again to reverse it. - Behind Browse's tiles, a library shows a slowly drifting wall of its own posters, Watchlist and History a row of theirs, Collections one collection with the films of it you have, and Surprise me a blurred wall. - A person's page matches the Apple TV app 2.0: their photo, the part they played, how many credits they have and over which years, and a Filmography button listing every credit by year. All of their credits now appear, where only the first 30 used to. - Show posters say how many episodes you have left, and finished titles carry a tick; Watched marks in Settings turns the ticks off. A title without a tofa score shows its TMDB rating instead. - Hidden episodes follow the Apple TV app: past the first one you have not seen, each you have neither started nor finished keeps its details hidden. - History shows each film or show once, with its year and rating. - Who's watching matches the Apple TV app 2.0: profiles three to a row on a plain background, in your fox's colour, with the app's PIN pad. - New in Settings: Pause screen (turn it off to keep the controls up while paused) and Reduce motion (no zooms, slides or moving backgrounds). - Down from the top bar now works straight away when you move on from Home before it has finished loading. - After updating, tofa asks once to add a new font to your skin.

extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Needs tofa media server 0.11.0 or newer. An older server still works, but you are told once per session that some screens may be incomplete. - Search now finds collections of every kind: your own, film series like James Bond, and tofa's curated sets. The best match appears as a row of the titles you have, just below the top result. - More Like This no longer waits and asks again when a title has nothing similar; the server now says so straight away. - Browse a library by its folders: a View button at the start of the row switches between the library's own view and Folders. Libraries of home videos open in Folders. Back goes up a level, and selecting the library again returns to its top. - A film or episode split across several files now plays as one: one timeline over all its parts, and no picking between "versions" that are really part 1 and part 2. - Cast and crew photos now load from your own server. - Dolby Vision Profile 5 videos are converted on devices without Dolby Vision, instead of playing in the wrong colours. - Picture subtitles on a converted stream can be chosen again before the server has prepared them; they appear once it has the whole track.

extension.summary: Fonts for the tofa for Kodi add-on
extension.description:
The typefaces the tofa for Kodi add-on draws its own screens in: Inter Tight, Roboto Mono and the Lucide icon set.
Installed automatically as a dependency of tofa for Kodi. It provides font files and nothing else: no screens, no settings, and nothing runs. It is not useful on its own.
Kodi looks inside enabled font resources for any font file it cannot find in the active skin, so tofa's screens can name these files without a copy of them being placed in the skin.
